title: Chicken Cacciatore
subtitle: Italian hunter's braised chicken with tomatoes and olives
excerpt: The Italian hunter's chicken: bone-in chicken pieces braised in a rustic sauce of tomatoes, olives, capers, anchovies, and white wine until the meat is deeply flavoured and falling from the bone. The sauce is as important as the chicken.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pollo alla cacciatora (hunter's chicken) is one of the most widely known Italian braises. The name refers to the style of cooking associated with hunters: braised with whatever aromatic vegetables, wine, and pantry items were on hand. Versions differ considerably by region: in the north, cream, mushrooms, and white wine are more common; in the south, olives, capers, and anchovies. The version here draws on the southern tradition. The anchovies dissolve into the sauce without making it fishy; they add depth and umami. Bone-in chicken pieces are essential: they flavour the sauce better than boneless chicken and remain moist through the long braising time.

content.text: Brown the chicken skin-side down in batches; do not move it until it releases from the pan easily. The browned skin adds colour and flavour to the sauce. Keep the braise at a gentle simmer: hard boiling toughens the chicken.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on thighs; or use a mix of thighs and drumsticks

content.text: Season the chicken with salt. Heat the olive oil in a wide casserole over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 8 minutes without moving until the skin is deep golden. Turn and brown the other side for 3 minutes. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat. Cook the onion in the pan for 5 minutes until soft. Add the anchovies and stir until they melt into the oil. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, rosemary, and bay leaves.

Return the chicken pieces skin-side up. Add the olives and capers. Cover and simmer over low heat for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and very tender. Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes to reduce the sauce. Remove the bay leaves. Scatter with parsley and serve with polenta, crusty bread, or pasta.
